instantiated_cells.justification: The code defines covered lobbying activity as direct communications to promote/advocate/oppose legislation (§101.70(E)), contacts to influence an executive agency decision (§121.60(I)), and contacts to influence a retirement system decision (§101.90(I)).

Each of the three lobbyist categories is defined as a natural person ("any individual" legislative agent; "any person" executive agency lobbyist; "any person" retirement system lobbyist), not as an entity.

"Person" expressly includes state instrumentalities and political subdivisions (counties, townships, municipal corporations, school districts, etc.), which is a statutory definition encompassing public entities.
Both "executive agency lobbyist" and "retirement system lobbyist" require lobbying as a main purpose on a "regular and substantial basis," which functions as a materiality/substantiality threshold.

Executive agency lobbying is defined as contacts to influence an "executive agency decision" by communicating with specified executive-branch officials, and "executive agency" is defined in §121.60(F).
The executive-agency lobbying definitions and expenditure coverage include "a member of the staff" of listed executive officials, and "staff" is defined in §121.60(M).

Legislative lobbying targets include the governor and governor's staff (§101.70(D),(E)), and executive-agency lobbying targets include the governor as an "elected executive official" (§121.60(B),(L)).

"Legislation" includes matters pending before the controlling board (§101.70(B)), and legislative lobbying/expenditure definitions include communications with and expenditures to controlling board members (§101.70(D),(E)).

"Legislation" is defined as matters pending before the general assembly and related actions (§101.70(B)), and "actively advocate" requires direct communication with members of the general assembly (§101.70(E)).
Legislative lobbying includes communications with and expenditures to "any member of the staff" of listed officials (§101.70(D),(E)), and "staff" is defined in §101.70(J).

Each lobbyist definition excludes certain elected/appointed officials (e.g., members of the general assembly and elected executive officials in §101.70(F); officers/employees of agencies in fiduciary capacity in §121.60(H) and §101.90(H)), showing the statute addresses elected officials as an actor class in defining who is (not) a lobbyist.

The lobbyist definitions expressly carve out public officers/employees acting in a fiduciary capacity or holding specified public positions, thereby treating public employees as an actor class for definitional purposes.
The definition of "person" includes enumerated governmental units and instrumentalities but does not condition inclusion on being chartered or incorporated by a government.
Nothing in the enumerated public-entity inclusions (state instrumentalities and political subdivisions) turns on government ownership or ownership percentage.
The statute's public-entity coverage is based on the entity being a state instrumentality or political subdivision, not on revenue sources such as public funding percentages.
